conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: Execution
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule text: 'When the data items are not described by the same data description entry, the result of the statement is undefined.' (cite.py --check 14.6.10 -> OK, rule 1). The rule states NO required result, so every behavior conforms; there is no expected value to compute and no golden may pin one (cf. the owner-signed DRV-GR-14.9.20.4-9 treatment of the sibling INITIALIZE GR9 in CONFORMANCE.md §8). COBOL.NET's behavior is determinate (typed-native stores: the sending value is rendered then stored). CONFORMS-but-untested is the expected outcome for an undefined-result rule. || editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (§14.6.10 is not an Annex E change)
rows.rule-text: When the data items are not described by the same data description entry, the result of the statement is undefined.

rows.subject: Execution
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'When the data items are described by the same data description entry, the result of the statement is the same as if the data items shared no part of their respective storage areas.' (cite.py --check 14.6.10 -> OK, rule 2). Items described by the SAME entry can only share storage by being the same occurrence (full overlap), so the obligation is that a statement reads its sending value before it stores. Probe E:\Temp\claude\E--CobolSharp\a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec\scratchpad\adj-d1\out\probe\ovl\ovl.cob (pinned cobol.exe, --std 2023) - every result equals the no-overlap result: ADD A TO A (7) -> 0014; MULTIPLY B BY B (3) -> 9; COMPUTE C = C*2 + C/5 (5) -> 11.00; MOVE E(I) TO E(J), I=J=2 -> XYZ042 unchanged; MOVE G TO G -> ABCD1234; SUBTRACT N FROM N GIVING N -> 0; DIVIDE N INTO N -> 1; ADD N N N TO N (10) -> 40; ADD 1 TO N GIVING N N -> 11. Arithmetic is also covered by §14.7.7 rule 4 a)/NOTE 3 (the intermediate is complete before any store; cite.py --check 14.7.7 -> OK). The reference-modification sentence ('not considered to be the same data description entry ... undefined') imposes no result. No existing spec-derived test names this rule.
rows.rule-text: When the data items are described by the same data description entry, the result of the statement is the same as if the data items shared no part of their respective storage areas. NOTE 1 The execution of a statement can have side effects on implicitly referenced items. When such items share a part or all of their storage areas with other explicitly or implicitly referenced items, there can be unexpected results. Similarly, when the rules for a statement explicitly or implicitly specify or reference multiple receiving operands, and some or all of those receiving operands share a part or all of their storage areas, there may be unexpected results among those receiving operands. NOTE 2 The impact of overlapping operands for both implicit and explicit references is discussed in D.5, Sharing of storage among data items. In the case of reference modification, the unique data item produced by reference modification is not considered to be the same data description entry as any other data description entry. Therefore, if an overlapping situation exists, the results of the operation are undefined.

rows.subject: Execution
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'When a SORT or MERGE statement is executed, an implicit transfer of control occurs to any associated input or output procedures.' (cite.py --check 14.6.3 -> OK, rule 2). Probe E:\Temp\claude\E--CobolSharp\a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec\scratchpad\adj-d1\out\probe\xfer\xsort.cob: SORT SF ... INPUT PROCEDURE IS IN-PROC OUTPUT PROCEDURE IS OUT-PROC -> the input procedure's RELEASEs of CCC/AAA/BBB and the output procedure's RETURN loop print OUT AAA / OUT BBB / OUT CCC then O2-LAST then AFTER-SORT. Probe xmerge.cob: MERGE MF ... USING F1 F2 OUTPUT PROCEDURE IS OUT-PROC -> OUT AAA/BBB/CCC/DDD, O2-LAST, AFTER-MERGE. Both transfers happen. Many SORT/MERGE goldens exercise the procedures (e.g. pb349_sort_merge_flow_ec) but none is derived for THIS rule, so test-ref is left empty.
rows.rule-text: When a SORT or MERGE statement is executed, an implicit transfer of control occurs to any associated input or output procedures.

rows.subject: Execution
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (many sentences; cite.py --check 14.6.3 -> OK, rule 3 and the following paragraphs). Verified sentence by sentence with the pinned cobol.exe: (a) transfer to exception procedures - xsort.cob's USE and xfatal.cob's USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION EC-SIZE both run. (b) 'EXIT PROGRAM causes an explicit transfer of control only when the statement is executed in a called program' - xexit.cob (a main program) prints BEFORE then AFTER-EXIT-PROGRAM at 85 and 2023 (a CONTINUE, matching Annex F.1 item 1's description). (c) a procedure with no statements acts as CONTINUE - xfer.cob PERFORM P5 (empty paragraph) -> M4; PERFORM S3 (empty section) -> M7; GO TO P5 falls through into S2 -> S2A S2B. (d) no next executable statement after the last statement of a source element not under control of another statement, and a program with no procedure division statements -> implicit GOBACK: CALL "SUBX" (falls off its end) returns -> SUBX M5; CALL "SUBE" (empty PROCEDURE DIVISION) returns -> M6; the main falling off its end after GO TO P5 ends the run unit, exit 0. (e) fatal-EC declarative with no next executable statement -> abnormal termination: xfatal.cob >>TURN EC-SIZE CHECKING ON, COMPUTE X = X / Z (Z=0) -> BEFORE, DECL-RAN, 'abnormal run-unit termination: EC-SIZE-ZERO-DIVIDE (fatal)', exit 1, AFTER-FATAL never printed. (f) the second fatal-declarative case - the declarative's last statement within the range of an active PERFORM executed in a different section and not the PERFORM's exit: xfatal2.cob, MAIN does PERFORM PX (section S2) whose COMPUTE X = X / Z raises the fatal EC -> BEFORE, DECL-RAN, abnormal termination exit 1; neither AFTER-FATAL-IN-PX nor AFTER-PERFORM prints (control does not return to the PERFORM). No test derived for this rule as a whole. || editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the EC-declarative sentences are 2002+; EXIT PROGRAM is ARCHAIC at 2023, Annex F.1)
rows.rule-text: When any COBOL statement is executed that results in the execution of exception processing procedures, an implicit transfer of control to those procedures occurs as specified in 14.6.13.1, Exception conditions. NOTE Another implicit transfer of control occurs after execution of the exception processing procedures as specified in 14.6.13.1.3, Fatal exception conditions and 14.6.13.1.4, Nonfatal exception conditions. An explicit transfer of control may be caused only by the execution of a procedure branching or conditional statement. The procedure branching statement EXIT PROGRAM causes an explicit transfer of control only when the statement is executed in a called program. If control is transferred either implicitly or explicitly to a procedure containing no statements, execution proceeds as if the procedure contained only a single sentence consisting of a CONTINUE statement. In this document, the term 'next executable statement' is used to refer to the next COBOL statement to which control is transferred according to the rules above and the rules associated with each language element. There is no next executable statement when the execution of an EXIT PROGRAM, GOBACK, or STOP statement transfers control outside the COBOL source element. In the declarative section for a fatal exception condition, there is no next executable statement after either the last statement when the paragraph in which it appears is not being executed under the control of some other COBOL statement, or the last statement when the statement is in the range of an active PERFORM statement executed in a different section and this last statement of the declarative section is not also the last statement of the procedure that is the exit of the active PERFORM statement. In these cases, unless the exception occurs in a MERGE statement, a SORT statement, or an I-O statement for which the implementor specifies otherwise, the run unit is terminated abnormally as specified in 14.6.12, Abnormal run unit termination. There is also no next executable statement after the last statement in a source element when the procedure in which it appears is not being executed under the control of some other COBOL statement in that source element, after the end marker, and when there are no procedure division statements in a program, function, or method. In these cases, an implicit GOBACK statement without any optional phrases is executed.

Probe E:\Temp\claude\E--CobolSharp\a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec\scratchpad\adj-d1\out\probe\iid\iid4.cob: MOVE FUNCTION STRF(FUNCTION CTR:1) TO X, where STRF and CTR each ADD 1 to an EXTERNAL counter K (0) and STRF returns 'wxyz' -> X='x', K=2: the function-identifier is evaluated (K=1) before the reference modifier's start (CTR -> 2), exactly as §14.6.4 orders it. rows.subject: Expressions
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule 4 (cite.py --check 8.8.2 "The two operands in a binary boolean operation shall not both be the figurative constant ALL literal" -> OK §8.8.2 4)). MakeBoolBinary reports COBOLNET1511 when both operands are BoundBoolAll{IsAllLiteral:true}; figurative ZERO carries IsAllLiteral=false (kb/Work PB157, landed) so `ZERO B-AND ALL B"1"` is legal. PROBE N01 `ALL B"1" B-AND ALL B"0"` -> COBOLNET1511 citing rule 4; p1b `A B-XOR ALL B"10"` = 0110 accepted. The check is in the one resolver callback, so it rides every site (COMPUTE, conditions, arguments). No test exercises the prohibition (grep of tests for the 1511 rule-4 message: none) -> test-ref empty. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2002, 2014, 2023 (boolean expressions and B-AND/B-OR/B-XOR/B-NOT are a COBOL-2002 introduction - the in-repo 2023 text's Annex E carries only the 2014->2023 delta, so the 2002 introduction is taken from the clause's absence in 85 and the probe gate COBOLNET0900 at --std 85)
rows.rule-text: The two operands in a binary boolean operation shall not both be the figurative constant ALL literal.

rows.subject: FACTORY paragraph
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py --check 11.4.3 "Interface-name-1 shall be the name of an interface specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph of the containing class definition" -> OK §11.4.3 1)). Code: Build's CaptureImplements resolves each FACTORY IMPLEMENTS name through OoNameResolution.Resolve(Want.Interface) against the CLASS definition's REPOSITORY scope, COBOLNET0840 citing ISO §11.4.3 SR1. Probes: p1 - FPI defined in the group and in the PROGRAM's repository but NOT the class's -> COBOLNET0840 '(FACTORY): IMPLEMENTS FPI ... not declared in the REPOSITORY paragraph ... (ISO §11.4.3 SR1)'; p8 - IMPLEMENTS names a CLASS (FPC, in the class REPOSITORY) -> COBOLNET0840 'no such an interface' (both halves: 'an interface' and 'specified in the REPOSITORY'). Legal cases (p5/p6) accepted. No existing test exercises the FACTORY arm (OoClassTablePositionTests INTERFACES covers the OBJECT arm's 0840 only) -> test-ref empty (test-needed). Cosmetic only: the 0840 message reads 'no such an interface'. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002, 2014, 2023 (OO - the FACTORY paragraph - is new in ISO/IEC 1989:2002; absent from 1985; Annex E of 2023 lists no change to §11.4)
rows.rule-text: Interface-name-1 shall be the name of an interface specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph of the containing class definition.

rows.subject: FACTORY paragraph
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py --check 11.4.3 "such that the factory interface of this class conforms to all implemented interfaces" -> OK §11.4.3 2)). Code: ValidateImplements runs Check(cls, ImplementsClosure(cls, factory:true), factory:true): for every prototype of every closure interface (AllPrototypes incl. inherited) it looks up the FACTORY roster (FindFactoryMethod walks the base chain, so inherited factory methods count) and applies §9.3.8.2.3 via MethodConformanceMismatches; missing or non-conforming -> COBOLNET0841. Probes: p2 - FACTORY IMPLEMENTS FPI with no factory SPEAK (instance has one) -> 0841 'the factory interface FPI requires a method SPEAK' (no cross-roster leak); p3 - factory SPEAK formal PIC 9(8) vs prototype 9(4) -> 0841 §9.3.8.2.3 rules 2/3; p4 - SPEAK inherited from base FPB's factory satisfies FPI (runs BASE-F 0042). Diagnostic cites §9.3.11/§9.3.8.2.3 rather than §11.4.3 SR2 (the operative clauses; acceptable). Existing 0841 tests (OoSpineTests.Implements_NumericDescriptionMismatch_0841 / Implements_MissingMethod_0841, MethodOmittedArgumentTests.Implements_OptionalPresenceDiffers_0841) exercise the OBJECT arm only -> test-ref empty (test-needed for the factory arm). || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002, 2014, 2023 (OO - the FACTORY paragraph - is new in ISO/IEC 1989:2002; absent from 1985; Annex E of 2023 lists no change to §11.4)
rows.rule-text: Each method prototype in each implemented interface shall be such that the factory interface of this class conforms to all implemented interfaces.

rows.subject: FILE-CONTROL entry, ASSIGN clause (consistency rules for external file connectors)
rows.adjudicator-notes: Corrected row (kb/Work/PB1530 'Decide, then make ONE of them true': the row now states the resolved-target rule the code implements). §12.4.5.3 1) b) and 3) b) (cite.py OK). Refuter: the rule compares the operand text (AssignTargetRule.Resolve output, uppercased), NOT the item-71 host path - probe /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s3/refute-probe/x4.cob: ASSIGN TO XADAT vs ASSIGN TO "xadat.txt" (both resolve to host file xadat.txt) -> EC-EXTERNAL-FILE-MISMATCH; row corrected to say so. Comparing the operand rather than the clause text is within the latitude §12.4.5.3 1) b) grants ('The implementor shall specify the consistency rules'), so PB1530 is a documentation defect closed by this row. The fingerprint is 'ASSIGN='+FileModel.AssignTarget.ToUpperInvariant() (AssignTargetRule.Resolve drops a DISK/PRINTER class and decodes a literal) plus 'USING='+name and qualifiers joined with OF, uppercased. Probes /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s3/probe/e1..e9.cob (two separately-described programs, >>TURN EC-EXTERNAL-FILE-MISMATCH CHECKING ON in both): "xa.dat" vs "xb.dat" -> EC-EXTERNAL-FILE-MISMATCH (fatal) at the CALL; DISK "xa.dat" vs "xa.dat", PRINTER vs DISK, XADAT vs "xadat", "Data.txt" vs "data.txt", FNAME IN G vs FNAME OF G -> no condition; FNAME vs FNAME OF G and TO "xa.dat" USING FNAME vs USING FNAME -> mismatch; e9 without >>TURN -> no condition. The old Pinned-by tests do not drive the ASSIGN arm with checking on (pb673 has no >>TURN; ec_external_file_mismatch differs in ORGANIZATION), so Pinned-by is empty; the witness PB1530 asks for is still owed.
rows.rule-text: FILE-CONTROL entry, ASSIGN clause (consistency rules for external file connectors). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (12.4.5, File control entry, General rule 1)
